originalTitle: 5 Energy ETFs That Have Soared in 2026
summary: Freight, gasoline, crude oil and broad-energy ETFs have delivered triple- and even four-digit gains in 2026 as the Iran war has driven energy and shipping prices sharply higher.
content:
With three quarters of the current year in the books, the U.S. stock market is on track for a fourth consecutive year of double-digit gains, with massive AI infrastructure spending coupled with exceptionally strong corporate earnings growth giving the market a major boost. The S&P 500 has returned 11.8% year-to-date, with only Utilities (-7.7%), Consumer Discretionary (-6.3%), and Financial Sector (-2.5%) still in the red. Hardly surprisingly, the Energy Sector has emerged as the top performer amongst the market's 11 sectors, managing a 37.4% YTD return compared to a 27.9% gain by second-placed Information Technology (IT) Sector over the timeframe.

However, the energy gains have not been uniform, with Oil & Gas stocks overperforming amid global supply shock triggered by the expanding Middle East conflict, while renewable energy stocks have underperformed.

Indeed, the popular fossil fuel benchmark, State Street Global Advisors Energy Select Sector SPDR Fun d (XLE), has returned 39.1% YTD while its clean energy peer, iShares Global Clean Energy ETF (ICLN), has notched a mere 3.1% gain. Energy stocks have been surging due to elevated oil and gas prices, surging power demand from AI data centers as well as a shift towards strict corporate capital discipline. 

However, energy exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have performed even better than individual energy equities thanks to many funds holding underlying futures contracts, shipping derivatives, or niche sub-sectors that capture soaring commodity prices directly, rather than relying strictly on corporate earnings.

Here are the best-performing energy ETFs so far in 2026.

#1 Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (BWET)

 Assets Under Management (AUM): $190.2M

The Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (BWET), issued by Amplify ETFs and designed by Breakwave Advisors, was launched in 2023 as the first ETF focused specifically on crude tanker freight futures. Unlike a traditional shipping ETF, it doesn't own tanker stocks. Instead, BWET holds Forward Freight Agreements (FFAs), essentially futures contracts tied to the cost of moving crude by sea, giving investors direct exposure to tanker rates.

That exposure has made BWET the standout ETF of 2026. Daily charter rates for Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs), the huge tankers used for long-haul crude shipments, jumped from roughly $75,000 to $100,000 before the Iran war to as much as $470,000 to $600,000 after fighting began in late February. Roughly 90% of BWET tracks VLCC routes from the Persian Gulf to China, putting the fund directly in the path of that surge.

BWET has also benefited from steep backwardation in tanker freight futures. In simple terms, tanker capacity today costs considerably more than the market expects it to cost several months from now. When BWET replaces contracts approaching expiration with cheaper later-dated contracts, it can capture an additional return from the difference, on top of the increase in freight rates.

There could still be upside, although after a roughly 4,000% gain this year, the bar is considerably higher. Gulf producers are moving more crude again, while ship-to-ship transfers and disrupted shipping routes require more tanker capacity to move it. If vessel availability tightens further, freight rates could climb again, while continued backwardation would provide another source of return. The reverse is equally important: if Hormuz traffic normalizes and tanker rates fall sharply, BWET has no fleet or charter revenue underneath it to cushion the decline.

#2 United States Gasoline Fund LP ETF (UGA)

The United States Gasoline Fund (UGA) offers one of the most direct ways for investors to bet on U.S. gasoline prices. The fund tracks RBOB gasoline delivered into New York Harbor, the benchmark used in the U.S. futures market, primarily by holding the nearest-month NYMEX gasoline contract. As that contract approaches expiration, UGA sells it and moves into the following month, maintaining continuous exposure to gasoline prices.

That exposure has paid off spectacularly so far this year as the Iran war disrupted global fuel supplies and pushed gasoline prices sharply higher. Unlike an investment in a refiner such as Valero or Marathon Petroleum, UGA does not depend on refinery margins, operating costs or corporate earnings. When gasoline futures rise, the fund gets the benefit much more directly.

There could still be upside after UGA's roughly 148% gain this year. Global fuel markets remain tight , while the Iran war continues to disrupt Middle Eastern supplies. Any further disruption to Gulf fuel exports or refinery capacity could push gasoline futures higher again.

The risk is that UGA is tied just as directly to gasoline on the way down, of course. A fall in fuel prices would feed quickly into the fund, while contango creates an additional problem. If later-dated gasoline contracts cost more than the contracts UGA is selling, the fund repeatedly has to sell cheaper contracts and buy more expensive ones as it rolls its positions. That can eat into returns even when the spot price of gasoline changes very little.

#3 United States Brent Oil Fund LP ETF (BNO)

 Assets Under Management (AUM): $645.8M

The United States Brent Oil Fund (BNO) gives investors direct exposure to Brent crude without buying oil producers or trading futures themselves. The fund primarily holds short dated Brent futures traded on ICE Futures Europe, moving from the nearest contract into the following month as expiration approaches. That makes BNO much more directly tied to the price of global crude than an oil stock, where returns also depend on production costs, hedging, taxes and company-specific decisions.

chineseTitle: 2026 年飙升的 5 只能源 ETF
chineseSummary: 由于伊朗战争推动能源和航运价格大幅上涨，货运、汽油、原油和广泛能源 ETF 在 2026 年实现了三位数甚至四位数的涨幅。
chineseContent:
今年已过去三个季度，美国股市有望连续第四年实现两位数上涨，大规模的人工智能基础设施支出加上异常强劲的企业盈利增长给市场带来了重大提振。标准普尔 500 指数今年迄今的回报率为 11.8%，只有公用事业 (-7.7%)、非必需消费品 (-6.3%) 和金融部门 (-2.5%) 仍处于亏损状态。毫不奇怪，能源行业成为市场 11 个行业中表现最好的行业，年初至今的回报率为 37.4%，而同期排名第二的信息技术 (IT) 行业的回报率为 27.9%。

然而，能源股的涨幅并不一致，在中东冲突扩大引发全球供应冲击的情况下，石油和天然气股表现优异，而可再生能源股则表现不佳。

事实上，广受欢迎的化石燃料基准——道富全球顾问能源精选行业 SPDR 基金 (XLE)，今年迄今已回报 39.1%，而其清洁能源同行 iShares 全球清洁能源 ETF (ICLN) 的回报率仅为 3.1%。由于石油和天然气价格上涨、人工智能数据中心电力需求激增以及转向严格的企业资本纪律，能源股一直在飙升。 

然而，能源交易所交易基金（ETF）的表现甚至比个别能源股票还要好，这要归功于许多基金持有基础期货合约、航运衍生品或直接捕捉大宗商品价格飙升的利基子行业，而不是严格依赖企业盈利。

以下是 2026 年迄今为止表现最佳的能源 ETF。

#1 Breakwave 油轮运输 ETF (BWET)

管理资产 (AUM)：1.902 亿美元

Breakwave 油轮运输 ETF (BWET) 由 Amplify ETFs 发行并由 Breakwave Advisors 设计，于 2023 年推出，是首个专门专注于原油油轮货运期货的 ETF。与传统的航运 ETF 不同，它不拥有油轮股票。相反，BWET 持有远期运费协议 (FFA)，本质上是与海上原油运输成本挂钩的期货合约，让投资者可以直接接触油轮费率。

这种风险使 BWET 成为 2026 年表现出色的 ETF。超大型原油运输船 (VLCC)（用于长途原油运输的大型油轮）的日租费从伊朗战争前的约 75,000 美元至 100,000 美元跃升至 2 月底战斗开始后的 470,000 美元至 600,000 美元。 BWET 大约 90% 的资金追踪从波斯湾到中国的 VLCC 航线，使该基金直接处于这一激增的路径中。

BWET 还受益于油轮货运期货的大幅现货溢价。简而言之，目前油轮运力的成本远远高于市场预期几个月后的成本。当 BWET 用更便宜的较晚合同替换即将到期的合同时，除了运费上涨之外，它还可以从差价中获得额外的回报。

尽管今年上涨了约 4,000%，但目前的门槛已经相当高了，但仍有可能上涨。海湾生产商再次运输更多原油，而船对船转运和中断的航线需要更多的油轮运力来运输原油。如果船舶供应进一步紧张，运费可能会再次攀升，而持续的现货溢价将提供另一个回报来源。反过来也同样重要：如果霍尔木兹运输量恢复正常且油轮运价大幅下降，BWET 就没有船队或包机收入来缓冲下降。

#2 美国汽油基金 LP ETF (UGA)

美国汽油基金（UGA）为投资者押注美国汽油价格提供了最直接的方式之一。该基金主要通过持有最近月份的 NYMEX 汽油合约来追踪输送到纽约港的 RBOB 汽油（美国期货市场使用的基准）。随着该合同即将到期，UGA 将其出售并进入下个月，从而持续承受汽油价格的影响。

今年迄今为止，随着伊朗战争扰乱了全球燃料供应并推高了汽油价格，这种风险已经获得了惊人的回报。与瓦莱罗 (Valero) 或马拉松石油 (Marathon Petroleum) 等炼油厂的投资不同，UGA 不依赖于炼油厂利润、运营成本或公司盈利。当汽油期货上涨时，该基金会更直接地受益。

UGA 今年上涨约 148% 后，仍有上涨空间。全球燃料市场依然紧张，而伊朗战争继续扰乱中东供应。海湾地区燃料出口或炼油产能的任何进一步中断都可能再次推高汽油期货。

当然，风险在于，UGA 在下跌过程中同样与汽油直接挂钩。燃料价格的下跌将迅速流入该基金，而期货溢价又造成了另一个问题。如果较晚日期的汽油合同成本高于 UGA 出售的合同，该基金在展期时必须反复出售更便宜的合同并购买更昂贵的合同。即使汽油现货价格变化很小，这也会影响回报。

#3 美国布伦特石油基金 LP ETF (BNO)

 管理资产 (AUM)：6.458 亿美元

美国布伦特石油基金（BNO）为投资者提供直接投资布伦特原油的机会，而无需购买石油生产商或自行交易期货。该基金主要持有在 ICE 欧洲期货交易所交易的短期布伦特期货，随着到期日的临近，从最近的合约转向下个月。这使得 BNO 与全球原油价格的联系比石油股票更直接，而石油股票的回报还取决于生产成本、对冲、税收和公司特定决策。
